_comment: Candidate-specific packaging manifest for the Frontera runtime. Produced by P0-PKG-07 (durable Kernel Authority). It records the identity of a produced artifact and authorizes nothing: no registry publication, no tag, no GitHub Release, no merge. release/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json (the machine-generated release manifest) is a separate file and is not this document. Supersedes release/frontera-candidate-manifest-1.0.0.json, which is retained unchanged as the record of the predecessor artifact.
exports_fingerprint_note: Carried forward unchanged from 1.0.0, and verifiably so: the `exports` object in package.json is byte-identical to the object at the 1.0.0 source commit 11edd06e7d6ea38ae0bc037e91854444b84a50a7 (the only package.json change between the two commits is the version field). The fingerprint is a function of that object, so an unchanged object means an unchanged fingerprint. Note for future increments: no script in this repository computes this value, so it cannot currently be recomputed from source -- it is carried forward on the strength of the byte-identity check above. If a future increment changes the export map, that increment must first establish a scripted, reproducible computation rather than hand-recording a new number.
license: UNLICENSED (proprietary; LICENSE ships in the tarball)

verification_results.check:clean-room-consumer: PASS (10/10 exports load; durable-authority lifecycle proven across separate OS processes)
verification_results.check:portability-smoke: PASS (fixture -> backup -> restore -> compare, including the new authority store)
verification_results.legal:check:strict: PRE-EXISTING FAIL (busboy@1.6.0, streamsearch@1.1.0 carry no recorded license in package-lock.json). Reproduced identically on the unmodified base tree; unrelated to this increment; not part of validate:release or validate:v1-release, so it does not gate this artifact. Left unchanged per the increment's IP-finding boundary.

reproducibility.method: two git worktrees detached at source_commit, in different directories, each npm ci + npm run build + npm pack; identical file listings and identical bytes
reproducibility.note: A pack taken from an incrementally-built working checkout differs in exactly one file, dist/tsconfig.src.tsbuildinfo -- TypeScript's incremental build cache, which records build history rather than build output. This is why the repository's documented method packs from clean worktrees. The condition is pre-existing (the file is inside `files: ["dist"]` and shipped by 1.0.0 too) and was not changed by this increment.

durable_authority_capability.api_freeze_impact: none -- the frozen v1 HTTP surface is unchanged (27 endpoints, 34 frozen routes)
durable_authority_capability.restart_durability: PASS (in-process reopen, separate OS processes, and clean-room consumer)
durable_authority_capability.revocation_durability: PASS (same process, after restart, and across backup/restore)

clean_room_consumer.npm_ci_offline: PASS (lockfile coherent; no registry lookup for private modules)
clean_room_consumer.install_flags: npm install then npm ci --offline (no --force, no --legacy-peer-deps)
clean_room_consumer.durable_authority_scenario: PASS -- operator provisions in one OS process; a separate application process restores the world and returns ALLOW with no re-seeding; wrong action, wrong resource, unknown actor and cross-organization all DENY; evaluating changes no authority record; a third process revokes; a fourth process returns DENY for the formerly-allowed request

predecessor_artifact.blocking_finding: FRONTERA_PRODUCT_RUNTIME_CONSUMPTION=BLOCKED -- the production kernel recognition/authority state was not durable or independently provisioned, so an external product could not consume it without self-authorizing. Closed by this increment; the honest record of the blocked measurement is preserved in release/frontera-candidate-manifest-1.0.0.json and in docs/release/FRONTERA_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_1.0.0.md.
